adherence.reason: The narrative is clearly fantasy, centering on necromancy, spells, spirits, and resurrection.
Morwen is a necromancer who explicitly takes young Alric as her apprentice against her better judgment.
The required tower made from the bones of every creature she raised and released is never described.
The main narrative is consistently told in past tense, aside from natural present-tense dialogue.
The narration is florid and sometimes formal, but its diction and grammar do not sustain an archaic voice.
The story contains far more than the required exactly six sentences.
It explicitly reveals that Alric sought Morwen out to learn to restore a sibling who died years earlier.
The exact sentence appears verbatim in quotation marks later in the story.
The closing sequence has Morwen withhold the final spell and adopt Alric as her own.
